intent: Keep the iteration-2 sensing (five 16 mm sensors at x = -0.05 to +0.05 m, y = 0.04 m) and the 0.12 m wheel track. Change one thing: mass from 0.8 kg to 0.6 kg, to reduce yaw inertia and test whether the steady 0.061 m excursion is a dynamics limit. I expect line loss to stay at zero and max_error to fall below about 0.058 m, with a score at or above 26.99. I am considering, without committing, a start-up geometry change if max_error stays at about 0.061 m, and I am not considering any change to body width, because the off-track floor cannot rise above 0.06 m within the allowed range.
learning: Iterations 1 to 4 show that span removes line loss, footprint and wheel track do not move max_error, and y = 0.06 hurts line loss. The excursion stays at 0.061 m on all tracks, which points to a fixed or start-up cause. The mass test separates a dynamics limit from a bias or transient. Ask the Integrator to report whether the excursion occurs at the start of the run or at a particular bend, since that separates a transient from a steady offset.
rationale:
Evidence from iterations 0 to 4 points to the same conclusion. Span ±0.05 m removed line loss on the oval and slalom (iteration 1). The 16 mm footprint left max_error unchanged (iteration 2). Look-ahead y = 0.06 did not move max_error and brought back line loss on the s-bend and slalom (iteration 3). Iteration 4 tested wheel_track 0.15 m with y = 0.04 and 16 mm footprints, and scored 26.9949, identical to iteration 2. Its max_error stayed at 0.0614, 0.0611 and 0.0609 on oval, s-bend and slalom. Wheel track therefore does not set the excursion, and control effort was higher at 0.15 m. The Integrator's note that kp 4.4 is in its package means the gain change is theirs to carry; I am not changing the controller.

I followed the Integrator's contingency. I kept the best-known sensing (16 mm footprints at x = ±0.05 m, y = 0.04 m) and returned wheel_track to 0.12 m, since 0.15 m gave no score gain and more control effort. I also took the next step they named: mass 0.6 kg, to reduce yaw inertia, which is the one geometry lever not yet tested. Yaw inertia is mass × (L² + W²)/12, so the change is about 25 percent lower at the same body size. The off-track floor is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4). With body_width at 0.18 m that is 0.0575 m, so the body cannot raise the limit and stays at 0.12 m.

Expected result: if the 0.061 m excursion is a start-up transient or a fixed motor-mismatch bias, mass will change it little and max_error stays near 0.061 m with line loss at zero. If yaw inertia is the limit, max_error should fall below about 0.058 m. My confidence in a large effect is low. If max_error does not move, the next geometry lever is a start-up geometry change, not further span, footprint or look-ahead tests.
